sections.label: Business trust controller information
sections.summary: The Bill requires unlisted registered business trusts to obtain and maintain controller information and provide it to MAS and public agencies on request.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: The Bill introduces requirements for unlisted business trusts that are registered under the BTA to obtain and maintain information on their controllers, also commonly known as beneficial owners and to also provide such information to MAS and other public agencies upon request.

sections.label: CEO and auditor requirements
sections.summary: The Bill extends requirements to CEOs of trustee-managers and requires auditors of listed registered business trusts to seek MAS consent before resigning early.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: The Bill will extend such requirements to CEOs of trustee-managers, in recognition of the influence that they have on the affairs of business trusts.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: The Bill further introduces requirements for auditors of listed registered business trusts and their subsidiaries to seek MAS' consent if they wish to resign before the end of their term.

sections.label: Lower poll threshold
sections.summary: The Bill lowers the threshold to 5%, making it easier for unit-holders to call for a poll.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: The Bill lowers this threshold to 5%, making it easier for unit-holders to call for a poll on issues that they are most concerned with.

sections.label: Trustee-manager removal threshold
sections.summary: The Bill aligns the trustee-manager removal threshold with the lower REIT manager threshold of more than 50%.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: Business trusts are managed by trustee-managers and REITs are managed by REIT managers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: This external management model introduces governance risks such as potential conflicts of interest between the external manager and also unit-holders.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: Currently, a trustee-manager can only be removed by unit-holders by way of a resolution passed by not less than 75% of the voting rights of all unit-holders present and voting at a general meeting.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: For REITs, there is a lower removal threshold of more than 50% which applies.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: The Bill will align the removal threshold for trustee-managers with that of REIT managers.

sections.label: Loan repayment situations
sections.summary: The Bill makes clear repayment must be made in certain other situations, such as conviction, but does not state as much for regulatory action loans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Conditions outlined in the new section 27B of the Business Trusts Act and in section 163A of the Companies Act appear to apply when the loans are for defending civil or criminal proceedings but not when the loans are for defending against regulatory actions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The Bill makes clear that repayment must be made in certain other situations such as when the director is convicted in the proceedings but it does not state as much for this situation.

sections.label: Reasonable steps and section 52N
sections.summary: The new section 52K requires trustee-managers to take reasonable steps to identify registrable controllers, and the question asks for illustrations and clarification on section 52N.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The new section 52K requires the trustee-manager of a BT to take "reasonable steps" to identify registrable controllers of a BT.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Can	the Minister of State provide illustrations to guide these trustee-managers on what would constitute reasonable steps in the discharge of their duties?

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Also, can	the Minister of State clarify whether the new section 52N applies to someone who knows or ought to know that someone else may be a registrable controller?

sections.label: Removing trustee manager approval threshold
sections.summary: The Bill lowers the unit holder approval needed to remove a trustee manager from 75% to 50%.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: First, the Bill makes provision, captured in the revised section 20 of the Bill, that only a 50% majority, rather than the current supermajority of 75% of unit holders' approval is required to remove the trustee manager.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: This amendment corrects a longstanding, yet glaring discord between BTs and other related trust structures, notably real estate investments trusts (REITs), where only a simple majority was required for removing the manager.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Given the enormous power vested into a trustee manager within the BT structure, this change will re-enfranchise the average unit holder.

sections.label: REIT gearing and BT registration
sections.summary: REITs can only be geared to 50%, raising concern they register as BTs to avoid leverage rules.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: In contrast, REITs are only able to be geared up to 50%.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: This introduces a potential concern, where essentially REITs are registering as a BT to avoid the prudential stipulations related in part to excess leverage.

sections.label: REIT, family office, BT, donation figures
sections.summary: It states 2020 figures for REIT assets, family offices, listed BT market capitalisation and tax-deductible charity donations.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The REIT asset class has grown to $130 billion in 2020.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: As Minister Tharman shared in response to my Sengkang colleague, Louis Chua's Parliamentary Question, the number of family offices has also almost doubled between 2020 and last year from 400 to 700.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Our listed BTs now boasts a market capitalisation of close to $20.6 billion.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The amount of tax-deductible donations received by charities has even receded slightly, from a peak of $1.07 billion in 2018, to $1.01 billion in 2020.

sections.label: Private and non-profit financing public expenditure
sections.summary: It suggests allowing private and non-profit sectors to take on greater importance in financing public expenditures.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: What I am suggesting is that we could put these two together, we could allow private and non-profit sectors to assume greater importance in financing various public expenditures.

sections.label: Foundations depleting endowments for expenditures
sections.summary: It proposes foundations deplete endowments by funding approved fiscal expenditures until a closure date, creating an indirect wealth tax.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: To prevent such outcomes, we should insist that our foundations consistently deplete their endowments by funding approved fiscal expenditures until a stipulated closure date.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Foundations may retain some independence over their target expenditures, but these areas would be pre-selected by the Government.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: This will result in an indirect wealth tax that carries significant social capital, appealing to high net worth individuals' sense of agency, civic responsibility and earnestness.

sections.label: Enhancing intermediary functions for wealth hub
sections.summary: It states that enhancing intermediary functions is a logical next step as Singapore matures as a global wealth management hub.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: As we position ourselves to mature even more as a global wealth management hub, enhancing such intermediary functions is a logical next step.

sections.label: Trustee-manager removal threshold alignment
sections.summary: MAS proposes aligning the removal threshold for trustee-managers with that for REIT managers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: For instance, MAS has, in this Bill, proposed that the removal threshold for trustee-managers be aligned with that for REIT managers.

sections.label: REIT distribution and tax transparency
sections.summary: REITs must distribute at least 90% of distributable income to enjoy tax transparency, unlike BTs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: On the distribution of REITs, I just want to clarify that REITs must distribute 90% of the income in order for them to enjoy tax transparency.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: In fact, REITs are required to distribute least 90% of their distributable income to enjoy this tax transparency, where BTs do not enjoy any tax transparency and, hence, are not subject to similar requirements.

sections.label: Regulatory framework for BTs
sections.summary: MAS drew provisions from the Companies Act and REIT regime to design a framework for BT stakeholders.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: What MAS has done is to draw the most appropriate provisions from both the Companies Act and also the REIT regime to design a regulatory framework that addresses the needs of stakeholders in a BT.

sections.label: Loan terms for defending proceedings
sections.summary: The Bill requires specific repayment terms for loans defending civil and criminal proceedings, but not regulatory actions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: In the case of loans for defending against civil and criminal proceedings, the Bill requires specific terms to be placed on the loans, namely that the loan is to be repaid no later than 14 days of certain events occurring, such as if the director is convicted.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: However, similar loan repayment terms are not required to be included for defending against regulatory actions, consistent with the comparatively less severe nature of regulatory actions versus Court proceedings.

sections.label: Loan repayment on final conviction
sections.summary: The loan must be repaid per required terms if the director is convicted or judgment is final.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: The general position is that the loan will need to be repaid according to the required terms, as long as the director is convicted or judgment is made against the director and that the conviction or judgment is final.

sections.label: MAS guidelines on this
sections.summary: MAS intends to issue guidelines similar to ACRA's guidelines under the Companies Act.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: MAS intends to issue guidelines on this, similar to the guidelines issued by ACRA, under the Companies Act.

sections.label: BTA alignment and governance safeguards
sections.summary: The amendments align the BTA with the regulatory regime for companies and strengthen corporate governance safeguards of BTs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: It is also to help them to find ways in which to give to local causes as they gain familiarity over time with what is required in the landscape.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: We have, so far, stayed away from dictating the causes that high net worth individuals should give to an industry.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: We just do not want to be that prescriptive in that regard as we start to build up this ecosystem.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: These amendments will bring the BTA in alignment with the regulatory regime for companies, upon which the regulatory regime for BTs is based.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: It will also strengthen the corporate governance safeguards of BTs.
